S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: A persistent perception that one is useless or inferior to others.
subtypes.Self-Criticism: Excessively and repeatedly blaming oneself for past minor failures or flaws.
subtypes.Reduced Self-Efficacy: Distrust in one's own ability to perform tasks or solve problems.
subtypes.Chronic Sense of Inferiority: Persistently evaluating oneself lower in comparison to others.
subtypes.Lack of Self-Assurance: Continually feeling anxious and unsure about decisions or actions.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD, dysthymia) is a chronic depressive condition characterized by a persistently low or dysphoric mood lasting at least two years, accompanied by additional depressive features such as low energy, low self-esteem, poor concentration, or hopelessness. Unlike episodic major depression, PDD tends to be less severe day-to-day but more enduring, often beginning insidiously and becoming intertwined with the person’s sense of self and usual functioning. Many individuals with PDD maintain basic roles at work or school but experience significant subjective distress, reduced quality of life, and impaired social or occupational functioning. Clinically, it is distinguished by its chronic course, early and gradual onset, and the tendency for patients to view their long-standing mood as part of their personality rather than a treatable condition, sometimes with superimposed major depressive episodes (“double depression”).

patient.stressor: Alex’s low mood began to creep in during his second year of college, when he was juggling part‑time data work, upper‑division coursework, and applications for internships, all while commuting from Chandler to Phoenix. Over the next two years, he transitioned into a full‑time management analyst role while still trying to finish his degree part‑time, and the constant pressure to perform, hit deadlines, and prove himself as the youngest person on his team slowly eroded the enjoyment he used to get from soccer, hiking, and cooking for friends. He noticed that even after getting a job and some financial stability, the sense of heaviness and disconnection from his old routines never really lifted, and his careful planning spreadsheets started to feel like an exhausting obligation rather than a tool he enjoyed using. The condition became clinically significant when his consistent underperformance on a major workflow‑optimization project led to a frank conversation with his supervisor about his declining engagement, prompting Alex—at his mother’s urging after a subdued family gathering where he barely participated—to seek psychiatric care through his company’s employee assistance program.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel drained all the time, like I never have the energy to get through work or even enjoy the things I used to.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I just feel this dull heaviness in my chest, like a gray filter over everything, and even when something objectively good happens at work or with school I can’t really feel happy about it, just kind of numb and detached.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I sleep, I wake up feeling like I’ve already worked a full day, and by the time I’m halfway through my commute from Chandler to the office I’m exhausted enough that just answering emails feels like wading through mud.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.
S042.manifestation: I constantly tell myself I’m not as smart or capable as the other analysts or my classmates, so when I mess up on a project or get a mediocre grade it just feels like proof that I’m a fraud who doesn’t really belong there.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: When I think about the future, all I can picture is more of this same grind—commuting, spreadsheets, classes at night—and I honestly don’t see any real chance that I’ll ever feel different or enjoy my life again, no matter what I change.
